name: legal-skills
description: legal-skills is a public, executable playbook for U.S. utility-patent work: agent skills in the SKILL.md format — checklists, examiner and adversary protocols, intake questionnaires, and deterministic Python — that make a language model do the work a patent boutique currently invoices at several hundred dollars an hour. It ships three skills: patent-audit (a 316-item pre-filing checklist grounded in 35 U.S.C., 37 CFR, and the MPEP), patent-examine (a simulated USPTO prosecution loop with two independent simulated examiners), and patent-workaround (adversarial design-around testing). The pitch is explicit: most of what you were paying for was process, and process belongs in files. From gfodor, the engineer behind React VR and an early, vocal Claude Code power user.
highlights: 316-item pre-filing audit checklist, 105 items blocking, sourced against statutes, rules, and MPEP
Deterministic Python handles arithmetic, deadlines, and claim dependency graphs — models do not do math
Simulated USPTO prosecution loop requiring two fresh examiners to clear the same bytes
Adversarial design-around testing with fresh competitor subagents and an umbrella-classification gate
Explicit refusal surface: no filing, signing, or IDS — those stay with registered practitioners
curatorNote: The agent-skills gold rush has been about coding; this is the first serious attempt to displace a licensed profession with SKILL.md files. 184 stars in a day says the 'replace billable hours with markdown' pitch lands — and the disclaimers are refreshingly honest about what the skills refuse to do. Worth watching to see whether legal process becomes the next agent-skill frontier.
